programmes.t: The Very Best of The Ed Sullivan Show
programmes.d: Carol Burnett hosts a retrospective of the very best moments from The Ed Sullivan Show, featuring performances from some of the biggest stars of music and comedy, stories about the show, interviews from Ed's favorite performers, and so much more!
Comedy genius and Carol Burnett co-star Tim Conway discuss his movie, Long Shot, marriage, and horseracing. Hal Linden joins in.
Michael J. Fox talks Family Ties and marriage, Larry Miller does standup and Harry Lorayne will test your memory.
Steve Lawrence is back for more fun with Carol and company! Steve plays an unsuccessful comic whose wife (Carol) heckles him at home. Also: commercial spoofs; Tim at war, attempting to fire a cannon.
Tim Conway guests for the movie spoof "Sinful Woman", a presentation of the Lyle-hosted Tearjerker Theatre, taken from their library of "creaky film classics."
One of late-night TV’s great hosts, Tom Snyder confesses it’s hard being Johnny’s guest. Tom also describes his life in California and bites back at his many critics.

programmes.t: The Best of The Ed Sullivan Show
programmes.d: Ed Sullivan presents Jimmie Rodgers, Joe Bennett and the Sparkletones, Arthur Worsley, Anna Maria Alberghetti, Carol Burnett, and Paul Anka.

programmes.t: The Best of The Ed Sullivan Show
programmes.d: Ed Sullivan presents Petula Clark, Tom Jones, Alan King, Dee Dee Sharp, Ugo Garrido, Margot Fonteyn and Rudolf Nureyev.
Carol offers a trio of guests: Lucille Ball, Eddie Albert, and Nancy Wilson! Albert drops in on "Carol & Sis" as Roger's new, health-nutty boss; then, all three appear on "As The Stomach Turns."
Andy Kaufman brings jumping frogs, Lara Flynn Boyle talks Twin Peaks and Tony Randall covers current events.
Guests Nancy Wilson and Nanette Fabray are here for tonight's "As The Stomach Turns." And on "Carol & Sis", the siblings practice for their First Aid course on a resuscitation mannequin.
Imogene Coca and Vic Damone guest star in this episode, which features Imogene and Carol attempting to secure air travel at family rates, a look at taboo commercials, and "The Old Folks."
Tim Conway and Charo guest! In separate sketches, Tim plays a man at a unisex salon, a fellow trying to stay awake for a speech, and a journalist meeting "Chiquita" (Charo) and her mother (Carol.)

programmes.t: The Best of the Carol Burnett Show
programmes.d: Tonight's episode features Harvey and Tim as tipsy friends coming home from a night of carousing, and a spoof of The Arabian Nights.
Fellow late-night host David Letterman stops by to talk about muggings in New York and earthquakes in Los Angeles. Scot Morris also stops by.
Star Trek’s Dr. Spock -- Leonard Nimoy – presents Johnny with a pair of Vulcan ears. Comic Bill Maher goes off on the sexual revolution, women’s rights and his current romance.

programmes.t: The Best of the Carol Burnett Show
programmes.d: Guest star Joanne Woodward spends an evening with 'The Family' in this episode.

programmes.t: The Best of The Ed Sullivan Show
programmes.d: Ed Sullivan presents Tony Bennett, Ethel Merman, The Muppets, Vikki Carr, Albert Brooks, and Gary Puckett.
Not your typical leading man, Dennis Hopper talks about his unusual roles in Blue Velvet and Easy Rider, and his up and down career which began in his Kansas hometown.
Charles Grodin talks about working with “tough guy” Charles Bronson. Stand-up comedian Brad talks about the challenges of dating when you’re 6’9”.
On this episode, invisible dogs run amok in an obedience class, while insurance agent Carol pesters doctor Tim while he's on the job.

programmes.t: The Best of The Ed Sullivan Show
programmes.d: Ed Sullivan presents The Doors, Jack Benny, Yul Brynner, The Skating Bredos, Flip Wilson, Hugh O'Brian, and Robert Goulet.
Jack Benny doesn't enjoy Paris and Joe Namath doesn't understand politics. Elke Sommer also appears.

programmes.t: Comedy Legends from The Ed Sullivan Show
programmes.d: Totie Fields' "Skiing"; Abbott and Costello's "Tax Collector"; Pat Henry's "Kid's Toys, Wife's Hair, Crazy World"; Wayne and Shuster's "Nursery School Rebellion"

programmes.t: The Best of the Carol Burnett Show
programmes.d: Maggie Smith returns to guest star as the erudite teacher of Eunice and Ed's son Bubba in another installment of 'The Family'
We're so glad we had this time together, but it's time to say "so long" as Carol closes the book on one of the greatest variety shows in television history.
Tim Conway and Steve Lawrence guest star, taking part in TV commercial spoofs. Tim also appears as The Oldest Man (now working as a dresser for the theatre), and in a pantomime sketch with Carol.
Carol is caught between two handsome men with Lyle and guest Robert Goulet join her for the Q&A. Sketches include the aftermath of a raucous party, and a maid entranced by a self-absorbed star.
Nanette Fabray returns as Carol's guest! Sketches include Carol and Nanette as a pair of precocious five year olds, and another episode of everyone's favorite soap opera, "As The Stomach Turns."
Guest Tim Conway proves that he and Harvey are one of the great comedy duos in a sketch where two mismatched policemen go undercover as a couple on a date. Also: a poker game on "Carol & Sis."
Buddy Hackett reads poetry and Cass Elliot makes one of her final TV appearances. Also appearing are firebreather Jan Munroe and artist Doug Kingman.
Big laughs are on tap with this episode, featuring the return of the world's oldest sex symbol, Mae East, to "V.I.P.", a Presidential "Fireside Chat", and a case of laryngitis on "Carol & Sis."
Guest star Jim Nabors walks the earth like Caine in "Kung Fu" in a supersized spoof of the hit David Carradine Western and Martial Arts television series, here entitled "Yung Fool."

Celebrated comic Richard Pryor shares his experience recovering from extensive burns and reminisces with comic George Carlin about starting out together in 1960s Greenwich Village.
Hollywood legend Carl Reiner stops by with his toupee. Plus, Jack Klugman talks examining dead bodies and Jan Todd shows you what it's like to be the strongest woman in the world.
